story_facts_verified.monthly_count: City of Columbus Building Permits open data (ArcGIS feature service, CC0 1.0), queried October 7, 2026: September 2026 demolition-type permits (GENERAL_TYPE ending 'Demolition') = 22, the highest of any 2026 month so far, versus a prior high of 18 (January and May), 17 in August 2026, and 17 in September 2025 (about 29% year-over-year increase). Full 2026 monthly series through September: 18, 3, 12, 10, 18, 7, 11, 17, 22 (year-to-date total 118). Permit type split: 8 commercial, 14 one/two/three-family.
story_facts_verified.geography: 22 permits covered 21 distinct addresses across 11 ZIP codes. ZIP 43205 (Near East Side) and ZIP 43224 (Linden) tied for the most activity, five permits each. The Near East Side cluster (1065, 1071, 1077, 1081 E. Livingston Ave. and 1088 Oak St.) totaled $317,061 in declared value, about half of the month's $644,011 citywide total; the largest single permit, $94,297, was the commercial teardown at 1081 E. Livingston Ave. In Linden, four separate single-family teardown permits at 4000, 4004, 4014 and 4022 Westerville Rd. all share parcel number 010104571, totaling $60,000. One outlier permit, $33,000 at 4691 Central College Rd. (ZIP 43081), sits on the city's edge toward Westerville.
story_facts_verified.historic_cross_check: Every September address was checked by point-in-polygon spatial query (maps2.columbus.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Schemas/Development/MapServer/18, the Historic Districts layer behind hub item 4fae82408663403499c387346437c56b_18) against the city's 18 historic districts; none intersected. A control point inside German Village correctly returned a match, confirming the query method. All 21 addresses were also checked against the city's PDF Register of Historic Properties (individually listed landmarks); none matched. The nearest listed property by street name, the Rickenbacker Boyhood Home (CR-28) at 1334 E. Livingston Ave., is a different, non-adjacent address not in this month's permit list.
story_facts_verified.original_contributions: A fresh ArcGIS pull of September's demolition permits with parcel-level grouping that surfaced the four-address/one-parcel Westerville Road cluster (not visible from an address-only read of the feed); a point-in-polygon historic-district check run this session rather than a visual map read; a cross-check against the city's individual landmark register (not run in the August format precedent) that also surfaced and ruled out the nearby but distinct Rickenbacker Boyhood Home listing; and a CREN bar-chart hero built from the same verified monthly series.
story_facts_verified.limitations_stated: The city updates its permit feed daily and late entries can still lift September's total; a declared value is the applicant's own demolition-cost estimate, not an assessed value or sale price; a permit is legal permission to demolish, not proof a building is already down; ownership and reuse plans for the Linden parcel and the Near East Side block are unknown and not asserted.
